html:
The Chaulukyas, or Solankis, ruled Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan from about 940 to 1244, from their capital at Anahilavada, today's Patan.

Mularaja founded the dynasty. Under Bhima I, Mahmud of Ghazni sacked Somnath in 1025, but the kingdom recovered quickly. Its rulers and merchants built some of India's finest stone work:

  • the Modhera Sun Temple, begun around 1026;
  • the Rani ki Vav, a royal stepwell at Patan;
  • the marble Jain temples of Mount Abu, paid for by ministers.

Siddharaja Jayasimha and Kumarapala ruled in the 12th century, with the Jain scholar Hemachandra at their court. In 1178 the Chaulukya army beat Muhammad of Ghor at Kasahrada. Power then passed to the related Vaghela family, which lost Gujarat to the Delhi Sultanate in 1299.
sum: The Chaulukyas, or Solankis, ruled Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan from about 940 to 1244, from their capital at Anahilavada, today's Patan.
